title: Why do static images sometimes look like they are moving?
hook: Do still images really seem to move for you?

narration.text: Sometimes your brain perceives movement in a completely still picture.
This is called illusory motion, a common visual illusion.
It happens because of how your brain processes visual information.
Our eyes scan the image, tiny movements causing light changes.
These quick changes trick motion-detecting parts of your brain.
Certain patterns and colour contrasts enhance this effect greatly.
Notice it next time you see a complex geometric design.
Has an image ever tricked your eyes into seeing motion?

description: Ever wondered why a still image sometimes appears to move? This fascinating phenomenon, called illusory motion, reveals how our brains interpret visual cues. Learn the simple reason behind this surprising visual trick.
topic: Why you sometimes 'see' movement in a static image, explaining the Illusory Motion phenomenon.
